title: Steady conduction through a steel slab whose conductivity falls with the temperature (EN 1993-1-2 curve), 20 and 700 at the ends
source: Kirchhoff transform of steady one-dimensional conduction with k(T): θ = ∫k dT satisfies Laplace's equation, so across a slab held at T₀ and T₁ it is linear in z; with k = a + b T the temperature is the root of a T + b T²/2 = θ(z) (H. S. Carslaw, J. C. Jaeger, Conduction of Heat in Solids, 2nd ed., Oxford 1959, §1.7). k is the library's EN 1993-1-2 carbon-steel curve, 54 − 3.33·10⁻² θ W/(m K) for θ in °C, linear over 20–700 °C

quantities.quantity: T at (0, 0, 50), the root of a T + b T²/2 = θ(z)
quantities.reason: exact discrete solution: θ = ∫k dT is linear along the slab, and with k linear in T a hex8 element's mean-temperature conductivity times its temperature gradient is θ's gradient, so the nodal temperatures are exact
